title: Evidence from a Multi-Regime Causal Discovery Benchmark: UCMT Algorithms, Comparative Performance, and Controlled Ablation Studies
abstract: arXiv:2611.26383v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: We present an internal, pre-registered evaluation of the UCMT causal discovery algorithm family alongside established alternatives across heterogeneous benchmark regimes, complemented by a separately pre-registered, controlled study of UCMT v2 Global components. The contribution is both empirical and methodological: a family-stratified comparison of three actively developed algorithm configurations and targeted evidence about which internal stages affect their outcomes. In the main benchmark, UCMT v2 Global has higher directed F1 than NOTEARS and DAGMA in selected real, semi-synthetic and Gaussian-network comparisons at the paired-run level, while trailing leading permutation-search methods in other settings. The BOSS-based UCMT v4 produces a CSuite-specific directed-F1 improvement over BOSS (mean paired difference +0.279; pair-level Holm p < 0.001), but the dataset-level adjusted result is not significant (p = 0.188). translated_title: 来自多机制因果发现基准的证据：UCMT算法、比较性能与受控消融研究
translated_abstract: 我们对UCMT因果发现算法家族与既有替代算法在异构基准机制上进行了内部预注册评估，并辅以一项单独预注册的、针对UCMT v2 Global各组件的受控研究。本工作的贡献兼具实证与方法论意义：对三个仍在积极开发中的算法配置进行了家族分层比较，并就哪些内部阶段会影响其结果提供了有针对性的证据。在主基准测试中，UCMT v2 Global在选定的真实、半合成及高斯网络比较的配对运行层面上，其有向F1分数高于NOTEARS和DAGMA，但在其他设置中则落后于领先的置换搜索方法。基于BOSS的UCMT v4在CSuite上相对BOSS取得了有向F1的改进（平均配对差异+0.279；配对层面Holm p < 0.001），但数据集层面的调整后结果并不显著（p = 0.188）。在另一项固定…（原文摘要至此截断）
tldr: 该论文通过预注册的多机制因果发现基准比较与受控消融研究，证明UCMT v2 Global在部分真实、半合成及高斯网络场景下有向F1优于NOTEARS与DAGMA，而基于BOSS的UCMT v4在CSuite上带来配对级显著改进，并揭示了影响算法表现的内部阶段。
en_tdlr: Through pre-registered multi-regime causal discovery benchmarks and controlled ablation studies, this paper shows that UCMT v2 Global outperforms NOTEARS and DAGMA in directed F1 on selected real, semi-synthetic, and Gaussian-network settings, while BOSS-based UCMT v4 yields a significant pair-level improvement over BOSS on CSuite, identifying which internal stages drive performance.
